Quick tech notes / clarifications for the run:

- Load profile: We'll model mixed RPS where 70% of requests are short (<128 tokens) and 30% are long chat windows (median 2.8k tokens). Burst windows: 30s ramps to 3x sustained RPS, hold 60s, decay 120s.
- Throughput target mapping: 1.5M tokens/day maps to ~17 tokens/sec sustained across the cluster. We'll size the harness for headroom (target 25 t/s during steady windows).
- Latency measurement: use end-to-end 95th on first-byte for generation; capture server-side generation time and client RTT separately.
- KV cache test: we'll warm caches with a sample of session traces Elena attached; then measure delta in token-generation latency and compute hit rate.
- Failure modes we will simulate: model fallback, node OOM (synthetic), and slow disk noise.

Karthik — can you confirm the harness will include a small stress injector for the node OOM noise and that the generated artifacts include per-request timestamps?

Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben/Team — confirmed. A few implementation specifics:

- Harness will publish per-request JSON lines with fields {ts, req_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, server_gen_ms, client_rtt_ms, cache_hit}. We'll attach the schema to the harness artifact.
- We'll run the baseline cluster from Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 unless Payline prefers self-run in staging VPC. Dedicated run will give us cleaner telemetry and simplified artifact collection.
- For node OOM noise we use a low-rate memory alloc loop in a separate container (non-intrusive) to create GC pressure; it will be toggled only during the third burst scenario.
- Pass/fail matrix (short):
  * p95 end-to-end <= 240ms for short requests (pass)
  * p95 end-to-end <= 850ms for long chat windows (pass)
  * KV cache hit-rate >= 60% after warmup (pass)
  * No more than 0.1% 5xx errors during steady-state runs

I'll attach the harness schema to the playbook. Monica — can you confirm the point-of-contact at Payline to hand off test credentials?

Karthik
